sentences.text: Devan Ramachandran, J
We cannot find approval with the contentions of the appellants in the appeal, which challenges the judgment of the learned Single Judge in W.P.(C) No.5840 of 2025.

2. Certain extent of land of the appellants were acquired for the purpose of Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL); and the appellants assert that they have received the compensation only to an extent of 0.21 ares of land, while they have been denied compensation for the balance of 0.43 ares.

3. According to the appellants, the taking over of the afore disputed extent of land for the purpose of the project is illegal, unless it had been notified under the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("Act" for short); and consequently that, they were constrained to approach this Court through the writ petition, seeking that such a notification be directed to be issued, so that they will get fair compensation for the said extent also.
4.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned Single Judge, however, dismissed the writ petition, finding that the disputed extent of 0.43 ares has, in fact, been 2026:KER:26821 surrendered by the petitioners in favour of the Kochi Corporation as early as in the year 2005 and hence being with no title or right over it thereafter.
5. Sri.

B.K.Gopalakrishnan - learned counsel for the appellants, conceded that his clients had preferred Annexure R3(d) application for relinquishment of land under the provisions of the The Kerala Land Relinquishment Act, 1958 ("Relinquishment Act" for short); but contended that this has never been accepted, nor has any formal order been issued by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO), as required under Section 4(5) of the said Act.

He predicated that, in the absence of such an order and since his clients are still paying tax on the extent involved, it has to be construed that they continue to be title holders and that no part of the same is vested with either the Corporation of Kochi or the Government.

6. Sri.B.K.Gopalakrishan - thereafter explained the reasons why his clients issued Annexure R3(d)
offer of relinquishment, saying that it was because they were under the impression that the land would be used for the purpose of the widening of the "Kaloor - Palarivattom"
Road; but that the said project never fructified and that it has now been taken for another purpose, namely for the KMRL.
He contended 2026:KER:26821 that, in such circumstances, the relinquishment of the extent could never have been found by the learned Single Judge to have competed.

7. Sri.V.Sethumadhavan, learned Senior Counsel, instructed by Sri.P.A Augustine - learned Standing Counsel for the 4 th respondent; and Sri.K.Anand - learned Standing Counsel for the additional 6 th respondent, submitted that the contentions of the appellants are wholly untenable and without any forensic basis because, once they had relinquished their rights over the extent of land in question,
they do not obtain any locus to claim that it be acquired as per law, or that they be offered compensation, for the reason that the land, as per the Relinquishment Act, vests with the Government or the Local Self Government Institutions, as the case may be.
They, therefore, prayed that the appeal be dismissed.

sentences.text:
We are afraid that we cannot find favour with any of the submissions of Sri.B.K.Gopalakrishnan for the singular reason that a learned Division Bench of this Court, in Natarajan R v. Village Officer,
Kanayannur Taluk and Others [2013 (2) KHC 26], has declared the law affirmatively that once a person offers relinquishment under Section 4 of the "Relinquishment Act", it operates against him,
even in the absence of a formal order having been issued by the 2026:KER:26821 Competent Authority.

entities.text:
Natarajan R v. Village Officer,
Kanayannur Taluk and Others [2013 (2) KHC 26]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We notice that the learned Single Judge has extracted paragraph No.8 of the said judgment, but we deem it necessary for our reading also, for which we also do as under:-
"On a reading of the above sections, we are of the view that the relinquishment by a registered holder as against him, operates unconditionally, on an application being made under the Act.
The act of relinquishment is a voluntary act of the registered holder which is unilateral and takes effect from the date of the application.
This is, for reason of the application being an expression of the intention to unconditionally surrender the possession and rights over the land to the Government.
The procedure contemplated is to ensure that no further claims are raised on the land by a third party on one count or another.
It cannot be gainsaid that if no order is passed, the land reverts back to the registered holder who had relinquished his rights.
If no order is passed, definitely by the relinquishment there is no vesting and cannot be final as against any thirdparty claiming title, possession or any other right over such land."
9. We are in full affirmation with the views of the learned Division Bench in Natarajan (supra) and obtain no reason to differ from it any manner whatsoever.

10. As far as the facts of this particular case are concerned, it is expressly admitted that the appellants had offered relinquishment of the disputed property through Annexure R3(d), as early as on 10.08.2005 and that they have never, at any point subsequent thereto, 2026:KER:26821 applied for the same to be revoked or cancelled.

It is only later, when the land was sought to be used for the KMRL, that they seem to have resiled, to make a claim that the said extent is also entitled to them,
with them being eligible to compensation.

We cannot find the learned Single Judge to have erred in any manner and consequently, the appeal is dismissed Sd/-
DEVAN RAMACHANDRAN JUDGE Sd/-
